title: First-order diagonal restriction is determined by the two axes
statement: Let $S$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $D=S[\varepsilon]$ be its dual-number thickening [def-sc-dual-numbers] over $S$. Let $X$ be any scheme over $S$ and $f,g:D\times_S D\to X$ be $S$-morphisms. Let $z:D\to D$ be the projection to $S$ followed by the zero section $S\to D$. If $f\circ(\mathrm{id},z)=g\circ(\mathrm{id},z)$ and $f\circ(z,\mathrm{id})=g\circ(z,\mathrm{id})$, then $f\circ(\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id})=g\circ(\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id})$.

source.place: Lemma 33.16.2 proof: square-zero pushout and epsilon_i mapping to epsilon; local arbitrary-ring form and group-unit-law application written out here

proof.text: Construct on double dual numbers the natural ring homomorphism x ↦ x.fst + inr x.snd.fst. Multiplicativity follows from square-zero multiplication. Whisker this natural transformation with the structure presheaf to obtain d:S[epsilon] → S[epsilon][delta]. Units are detected by the constant coefficient, which proves the induced stalk maps are local. Both composites with the two projections are identities, as checked on sections.

For f,g:S[epsilon][delta] → Y equal on the two axes, equality on the first axis identifies their underlying maps and their fst section maps. Equality on the second axis identifies their snd.fst section maps. For any ring map q from double to single dual numbers which is identity on each inclusion, q(inr(inr r))=0: express this mixed term as inl(inr r)*inr(inl 1), whose images multiply to zero. Expanding x shows q(x)=x.fst+inr x.snd.fst. Apply this formula to each structure-sheaf component of d to deduce equality of d followed by f and g. Scheme.Hom.ext concludes globally.

Let k:S[epsilon][delta] → D×_S D be the categorical lift of the two projections. Product extensionality and the dual-number identities identify the two axes followed by k with the categorical axes, and identify d followed by k with the categorical diagonal. Precompose the given f and g with k, apply the preceding sectionwise calculation using their axis equalities, and conclude equality in Over S by OverMorphism.ext.
